t.2.84.1: Seeing Bharadvāja's hermitage from a krośa away, that bull among men halted the entire army and went on together with his ministers.
t.2.84.2: For the one who knows dharma comes on foot alone, having laid aside his weapons and equipment, wearing two garments of linen, and having placed the family priest at his head.
t.2.84.3: Then, when Bharadvāja came into sight, Rāghava halted those ministers and went on behind the family priest.
t.2.84.4: Then, the moment he saw Vasiṣṭha, Bharadvāja of great austerities rose swiftly from his seat, saying to his disciples, "The guest-offering!"
t.2.84.5: Having met with Vasiṣṭha and been respectfully saluted by Bharata, the one of great splendor recognized him as the son of Daśaratha.
t.2.84.6: Having given the two of them water for the hands and water for the feet, and afterwards fruits, the knower of dharma asked them in due order about the welfare of their family.
t.2.84.8: Vasiṣṭha and Bharata asked him about his well-being: about his body, his sacred fires, his trees, his disciples, and the beasts and birds.
t.2.84.7: Speaking of Ayodhyā, the army, the treasury, the allies and the ministers, he did not mention the king, for he knew that Daśaratha had passed away.
t.2.84.9: Having agreed, saying "So be it," Bharadvāja of great austerities replied to Bharata with these words, out of the bond of affection for Rāghava.
t.2.84.10: What business brings you here, you who are ruling the kingdom? Tell me all of this, for my mind is not at ease.
t.2.84.11: I gave birth to him, the slayer of enemies, who increases Kausalyā's joy, and who, together with his brother and his wife, has been banished to the forest for a long time.
t.2.84.12: That greatly renowned one who, it is said, was commanded by his father, himself directed by a woman: “Be a forest-dweller here for fourteen years.”
t.2.84.14: Thus addressed, Bharata, his eyes brimming with tears from grief, replied to Bharadvāja in a faltering voice.
t.2.84.13: I trust you do not wish to do evil here to that sinless one and to his younger brother, with your mind set on enjoying the kingdom free of any thorn?
t.2.84.15: I am undone if even the venerable one thinks of me in this way. You should not suspect any wrong from me; do not, I beg you, speak to me like this.
t.2.84.16: What my mother said on my behalf was not what I wished. I am not pleased by it, and I did not accept those words.
t.2.84.17: But I have come to that tiger among men to win his favor, to bring him back to Ayodhyā, and to bow in reverence at his feet.
t.2.84.18: Considering me to be in such a state, you ought to show me your grace. Tell me, O blessed one, where is Rāma, the lord of the earth, now?
t.2.84.19: Bharadvāja, pleased, spoke these words to Bharata: "O tiger among men, born in the line of the Rāghavas, this befits you: devotion to your elders, self-restraint, and following the way of the virtuous."
t.2.84.21: Your brother dwells there on Citrakūṭa, the great mountain; tomorrow you shall go to that place, but today stay here with your ministers. O most wise one, skilled in the meaning of desire, fulfill this wish of mine.
t.2.84.22: Then Bharata, of noble appearance and joyful countenance, spoke the words, "So be it." And the son of the lord of men then resolved to spend the night in that great hermitage.
t.2.84.20: I know this is settled in your mind; I questioned you only so that it might be made firm, thereby greatly increasing your fame.
